spec.name: integrator-makes-whole
spec.intent:
Worktree /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share (branch design/first-share); every path below is under it and no command runs in the main checkout. Census @f2cd7e3a: the design was corrected there; plan architect-position is stopped under `design stability` and its landed architect-role and architect-skills work (7d53132e, e944facb, 9809add3, c076a864, ce240336, 539140df) is this unit's starting state. Re-derive any count or line below if a listed path changed since. Realize `integrator position`: the role that makes approved work whole. It takes each unit whose assay verdict is achieved, combines it with the work already approved, confirms the whole still holds by running the project's full check once so no implementer has to, returns a failure naming its unit to that unit's implementer by way of the architect, decides nothing about the design, repairs nothing, and leaves releasing the whole to the operator's sign-off. At census no role or agent holds it (note 'the integrator has no holder'); packages/canon/src/skills/deliver/skill.ts declares `integrator : P ⇀ agent` with no role behind it. Plan integrator-position's unit `integrator`, proposed and never built, is superseded by this unit.
THE LOOP (the contract the workflow units of this plan each state their own share of; the shards say what must hold, this is how). (1) The architect cuts a shard and dispatches the planner with it; the planner plans it and, when no plan is bound, binds it, returning only the plan's name. (2) The architect dispatches one integrator for the bound plan, named for the plan and kept warm across its waves where the harness can message a finished delegate (Claude Code: SendMessage to the name given at dispatch; omp: agent messaging); the integrator records each ready unit active as it hands out its address and returns only addresses, `<unit> of <plan>`. (3) The architect dispatches one implementer per address, naming the delegate after the unit and giving it the address and nothing it wrote itself. The implementer reads its spec, builds on its own branch, runs only its unit's own checks, commits its own work, and returns only `landed <unit> of <plan> at <commit>`, or `blocked <unit> of <plan>: spec` when the spec cannot be built as written (the architect routes that address to the planner). Its account of the work stays out of the return; what it doubts or meets beside the path it captures as a note. (4) The architect dispatches the assayer with the address and commit. The assayer reads the shard the unit realizes and the files at that commit, never the spec, and returns the assay verdict: achieved, or not achieved with what is missing in the design's own words, naming the unit and its implementer. (5) Not achieved: the architect sends the findings to the same implementer by the name it gave it, and the unit returns to (4). Achieved: the architect hands the address and commit to the integrator. (6) The integrator combines the unit onto the plan's integration line (a branch cut from main when the plan is bound, `plan/<plan>`) and runs the project's whole check once on the combined tree; no implementer or assayer runs it. Green: it records the unit completed, commits the records written since (plan, design, notes) by pathspec, and returns the unit as whole with the newly ready addresses. Red or a merge conflict: it leaves the line as it was and returns `red <unit> of <plan>: <failing check>`, which the architect sends to the same implementer. It never repairs, never reads to judge, and decides nothing. (7) When every unit is completed and the whole holds, the integrator closes the plan and asks the operator to release the line to main: a pull request where the repository has a forge remote and `gh`, otherwise the exact git command. It never moves main. (8) The architect never runs `plan show <unit>`, and never reads a spec, a diff, an artifact or an implementer's account; it runs no check and makes no commit or merge. Unit names reach it only as addresses, from the integrator and on verdicts. (9) Design stability. Every input, whether from the operator, a delegate or the architect itself, is a hypothesis the architect rectifies against its expertise and industry practice. A surviving change that bears on a shard the bound plan realizes is captured as a decision note on that concept's topic, blocking nothing; it is amended into the design only after that plan closes, and a following plan realizes it. A change to a concept no bound plan realizes is amended at once. Only when the architect finds the bound plan built on a shard that is itself wrong does it stop the plan: it captures a note blocking the plan (an owed ruling, so no unit is ready), corrects the shard once, and the planner rectifies the plan (repin, revise, retract, add) or rebuilds it; the architect then retracts the note and work resumes.
CHANGE. (1) New packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/integrator.ts, `export const integrator: Role`, in the form of its four siblings (arrow, stratum, reserves, prohibitions): reads the achieved verdict's address and commit, the plan's line and the plan; writes the line, the plan's state records and commits of records; reserves combine, whole-check once per combination, record active on hand-out and completed on green, close when every unit is completed, ask the operator for release; never writes an artifact (so the purview judge blocks a Write or Edit by this holder while its reserves pass the git and check acts), never repairs, never reads to judge, never moves main, decides nothing. The one-line report of (6).
(2) New packages/canon/src/roles/integrator.ts, `export const integratorRole: RoleCell`, mirroring roles/assayer.ts: skills ['deliver'] (deliver is the plan-side conduct of the loop; skill routing gives it with design, plan and note); guardrails [honesty]; actions [file-ops] (its vcs clause is this position's work); objective `delivery ⟨end-to-end integrated green⟩` (packages/canon/src/dimensions/objective/delivery.ts, which the architect left at census); capabilities without software-engineering (it does not build): verification-testing and operations-delivery; autonomy [mission-command] with no principal-self; satisficing satisfice; reasoning-strategy react; self-evaluation executable-test-oracle (it runs the check). Each choice carries a comment in its siblings' register. Routing tier is ruled (note 'the integrator's role-routing tier': omp task, Claude sonnet) and lands in unit claude-role-choice, not here.
(3) New packages/canon/src/agents/integrator.ts, `holds(integratorRole, { name: 'integrator', description, archetype, provenance: { mark } })`, mirroring agents/assayer.ts. The mark's emoji and hue are ones no other agent uses (census: 🏛️ blue, 🔬 red, 🔧 white, 🎬 magenta, ✈️ green, 📐 cyan, 🗺️ yellow). The description is the dispatch router's selection line and states the prohibitions out loud, following the assayer's 'NOT A REVIEWER' precedent: not a CI bot that fixes, not a release manager that pushes.
(4) docs/role.md: the position catalog names five positions, and one new section records the integrator: what it is, why it exists (the architect session did this work itself, the descent the architect position forbids), the plan's integration line against main as the release line, the operator's sign-off.
(5) .changeset/integrator-position.md (@cratylus/canon minor).
